name: What was taken, for how long, why, and how made whole

correction.previous: UEP-017 used a duration-of-enslavement fraction of a whole-life VSL
correction.replacement: Duration is a property of a specific deprivation, not the thing that defines restitution. Track a thing or right and its loss of use, and specify actual restoration.

remedy.preferred: restore original right or property first where feasible and appropriate

restitution_flow.rule: Identify the asset, entitlement or right and its owner, including Indigenous prior rights where applicable
Trace the action or chain of actions that removed or impaired it
Establish exact duration, including whether deprivation is ongoing
Inventory return in kind, prior credits and compensation already received
Specify a remedy matched to what was taken; do not substitute lifespan fractions
Confirm with the rightsholder or authorized successor that the proposed remedy addresses the proven deprivation
Record fulfilled, partially fulfilled, contested or unknown, not merely money promised

valuation.restoration_first: Return of land or right may be more appropriate than assigning a cash price
valuation.loss_of_use: Yearly benefits not received, net of actual uses and offsets; evidence required
valuation.replacement: Use appropriately evidenced replacement cost/value if return impossible
valuation.interest: Apply only defensible legally or economically specified interest to valid monetary flows at actual dates
valuation.vsl_13_1m: Human-life risk benchmark is a separate metric, not a generalized dollar principal

hypothetical_example.remedy: Restore parcel and lawful rights plus assess and compensate demonstrated net use loss, repairs and other distinct harms
warnings: $2,000 annually is an invented example, not an 1832 historical figure
The 40-acre illustration makes no claim of actual tract entitlements
Do not add full market land value if the same land was restored and no separate permanent loss established
If never returned, value of title and possession remain to be determined

historical_application.muscogee_1832: Treaty article entitlements, maps, title succession, forced removal, payment records and present rights; do not equate cession with consent or extinguishment of all claims
historical_application.slavery_1832: Identify labor extracted and benefits retained, freedom and property denied, transfers and inherited consequences without reducing all harms to years enslaved; no person-price assigned
historical_application.owners_trace: Differentiate dispossessed original landholders, enslaved rightsholders, purported owners and later grantees

progress.reason: Historic assets and repayment terms have not been fully traced for individual claims
